# SECURITY: auth handoff mints a full-JWT code for any destination the client names

- **Kind**: bug (security)
- **Date**: 2026-07-30
- **Requested by**: Ian
- **Source**: framework-side counterpart of Maestro Internal #941; scope reduced 2026-07-30 after review

Apply rules: django-mojo-build-conventions

## Description

`POST /api/auth/handoff` mints a code that `POST /api/auth/exchange` trades for a full
`jwt_login` — access **and** refresh tokens. The code records nothing about where it is
going, and redemption checks nothing but possession.

- `mojo-auth.js:864-873` — `requestHandoffCode()` posts an **empty body**. The client
  never names a destination.
- `rest/user.py:216-235` — `on_auth_handoff` takes no destination parameter, so the
  server cannot constrain one.
- `services/auth_handoff.py:27-41` — stores `{"uid", "ip"}`; `ip` is audit-only.
- `rest/user.py:238-257` — `on_auth_exchange` is `@md.public_endpoint()`.

The destination decision lives entirely in client-side JS reading the attacker-supplied
`?redirect=` param, so a crafted link opened by an already-signed-in user hands that
user's refresh token to any origin. `docs/django_developer/account/auth.md:174-178`
documents this as intentional and delegates the fix to deployments.

**Why it is worth fixing rather than documenting.** The fix removes a capability, it
does not add a speed bump: with the check at mint time the attacker needs a URL on an
allowlisted host that forwards a query string (a compromised tenant site, an open
redirect, an analytics beacon shipping `location.href`) instead of just an email. That
is a foothold you can find and fix versus a link anyone can send. It matters because
django-mojo is a framework — an identity/KYC product is built on it, and the most
click-susceptible population is gated-site members, not staff.

## Scope

**In:** the mint-side check, the client change that feeds it, and the `?back=` scheme
check (three lines, live XSS, same file).

**Out** (deliberately cut from the first draft, which was ~3x this):
- OAuth's `_validate_redirect_uri` prefix matcher — real, but a separate bug. The one
  live instance found (a downstream config with no trailing slash) is already fixed and
  pushed in that repo. File separately if wanted.
- `incident.report_event` on refusal — a `logit` warning is enough for v1.
- The four-file doc sweep — one section rewrite, settings reference, CHANGELOG.
- CSP — already filed as #945, and closeable as low value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/auth/handoff` requires `redirect_uri` and refuses (4xx, no code minted)
      unless it is allowed
- [ ] Fail-closed: nothing configured → cross-origin handoff refused
- [ ] Static matching is **exact host + path prefix**; `*.example.com` wildcard supported,
      one DNS label only
- [ ] A deployment can supply its own resolver instead of a static list (see D2)
- [ ] Same-origin / relative redirects are untouched — they never mint a code today
- [ ] `mojo-auth.js` sends the destination; a refused mint shows an error and navigates
      nowhere (today `auth_base.html:182-187` falls back to the raw target)
- [ ] `?back=` cannot carry a `javascript:` URL
- [ ] Tests: allowed mints; foreign host refused; confusable host refused; wildcard
      admits one label and refuses two; nothing-configured refuses; missing param 400;
      `?back=javascript:` regression
- [ ] Docs: rewrite `auth.md:174-181` (it documents the hole as intended), settings
      reference, CHANGELOG

---

## Plan

### D1 — Check at issuance, never at exchange

`auth/handoff` takes the destination and refuses before a code exists. Nothing spoofable
participates. Do **not** check `Origin`/`Referer` at `auth/exchange`: that request is
server-to-server from the consuming app's backend, which sets its own headers — an
attacker holding the code holds the headers too. `auth/exchange` is not modified.

### D2 — Configuration: static list OR a deployment resolver

Two sources, checked in order:

1. `AUTH_HANDOFF_RESOLVER` — dotted path to `fn(url, request=None) -> bool`, loaded via
   `mojo.helpers.modules.load_function()` and cached, exactly like
   `PRE_REGISTER_VALIDATOR` / `USER_LOGIN_HANDLER` in
   `mojo/apps/account/services/extensions.py`. When set, it decides.
2. `AUTH_HANDOFF_ALLOWED_URLS` — static list, for deployments that don't need dynamic
   destinations.

Neither set → refuse all cross-origin handoff.

The resolver is the answer to "we can't enumerate domains in settings". A multi-tenant
platform implements one function against its own domain registry — DB-backed, live, no
redeploy when a tenant adds a domain. The framework stays ignorant of tenancy. This is
an existing framework idiom, not a new mechanism.

**A resolver is security-critical code in the deployment.** Document it as such: it must
compare hosts exactly, must not substring/prefix match, and must fail closed on error.
The framework wraps the call and treats an exception as "refused" — unlike
`USER_LOGIN_HANDLER`, which swallows errors, a failing resolver must never open the gate.

### D3 — Static matching rules

Exact host (case-folded) **and** URL prefix. `*.example.com` matches
`host == base or host.endswith("." + base)` with a single non-empty dot-free label — so
`a.example.com` yes, `a.b.example.com` and `example.com.evil.tld` no. Scheme must be
http/https, which also refuses `javascript:`/`data:` (no hostname).

### Implementation steps

1. **`mojo/apps/account/services/redirect_allowlist.py`** (new, small) —
   `is_allowed_destination(url, request=None)`: resolver if configured, else static list
   per D3. Exception from a resolver → False, logged.
2. **`services/auth_handoff.py`** — `create_handoff_code(user, destination=None, ip=None)`
   stores `dest` for audit. Docstring: never enforced on consume, and why.
3. **`rest/user.py` → `on_auth_handoff`** — `@md.requires_params("redirect_uri")`,
   validate, refuse with `merrors.ValueException` (400) and a `logit` warning naming the
   refused destination. No code minted. `on_auth_exchange` untouched.
4. **`static/account/mojo-auth.js`** — `requestHandoffCode(destination)` posts
   `{redirect_uri: destination}`; rejects with no destination.
5. **`templates/account/auth_base.html`** — `redirect()` passes `target` to
   `requestHandoffCode(target)`; the `.catch()` at :182-187 shows
   `_mat.showMessage(…, "error")` and navigates nowhere.
6. **`auth_base.html:196-198`** — set `backEl.href` only for http/https or a same-origin
   relative path. Host deliberately not allowlisted; "back to the marketing site" is
   legitimately cross-origin and the scheme check is what closes the XSS.
7. **Tests** — `tests/test_auth/handoff.py`. The 11 existing endpoint tests post `{}` and
   need `redirect_uri` (test project allows `https://example.com/`). Add: allowed mints;
   foreign host refused with no code in the body; `example.com.evil.tld` refused;
   `example.com@evil.tld` refused; wildcard one-label yes / two-label no; nothing
   configured refuses; missing param 400; a resolver that returns False refuses and one
   that raises refuses; `?back=javascript:` regression.
8. **Docs** — rewrite `docs/django_developer/account/auth.md:174-181`; add both settings
   to `docs/django_developer/helpers/settings_reference.md` with the resolver contract
   and its fail-closed requirement; CHANGELOG (BREAKING: `redirect_uri` now required,
   fail-closed default).

### Deployment impact

- **Nothing outside this repo calls `POST /api/auth/handoff`** — verified by grep across
  every sibling checkout. The hosted auth page is the only minter, so no server-side
  integration breaks.
- **Consumers only redeem `?auth_code=`** (portal framework `TokenManager`/`PortalApp`, a
  product portal's `init.js`, one deployment's site-gate return leg). Unaffected except
  by whether the mint happens.
- **One deployment must configure before upgrading**: its gated-sites flow redirects to
  `<slug>.<wildcard-domain>`, which nothing allowlists today. Either a static
  `AUTH_HANDOFF_ALLOWED_URLS` entry with the wildcard, or a resolver. **This item does
  not ship until that config lands with it.**
- Deployments whose cross-origin destinations are already in `ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URLS` must
  still opt in explicitly — this item deliberately does **not** inherit that setting
  (dropped from the first draft: re-purposing a setting silently changes the meaning of
  values operators wrote under different semantics).

### Baseline

Per `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`: batch baseline captured once before any edit —
2959 passed / 1 failed / 385 skipped. The single failure
(`test_geofence > config: DELETE geo/rules removes the DB override`) passes 12/12 in an
isolated re-run; a known cross-module shared-state flake, accepted by the user at the
batch gate as the only pre-existing failure. Nothing in this item touches geofence.

### Review history

The first draft of this plan was red-teamed and then cut by roughly two thirds. What
survived from the challenge round:

- **Check at issuance, not exchange** — headers at exchange time are spoofable theatre.
- **Exact host + path prefix**, not host-only — host-only makes every path on an allowed
  host a token-deposit site (open redirector, query reflector, analytics beacon).
- **Wildcards confined to the new setting** — `urlsplit("https://*.example.com/").hostname`
  returns `'*.example.com'`, so inheriting `ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URLS` would have silently
  activated wildcards written when they were inert.
- **No "request's own host" rule** — `auth_base.html:71` shows `API_BASE` may be a
  different host than the page, and it would have sourced trust from the `Host` header.
- **A refused mint must not silently redirect** — the draft's `.catch()` sent users to the
  default destination with no error.
- **`?back=` is a live `javascript:` sink** — `auth_base.html:95` → `:196-198`, no scheme
  check, and no CSP anywhere in the framework.

Cut on cost/benefit review: the OAuth matcher change, incident reporting, group-metadata
sourcing, a test-mode override header, and the multi-file doc sweep.
